# v1 versus v2 (auto-generated by R/09_compare_versions.R)

Facts for the comparison section. Every number is computed from the saved
tables of both versions. Do not edit by hand.

## Design

- v1: 100 galaxies (80 train / 20 test). v2: 120 galaxies (100 train / 20 test).
- The 20 new galaxies come from a second, independent SkyServer pull with the same query (batch 2) and passed the same cleaning rules. They were added to the training set only; the 20 test galaxies are identical in both versions.
- New galaxies: z = 0.032–0.199 (median 0.094; v1 training median 0.101). KS test against the v1 training set: redshift p = 0.68, g − r p = 0.10, so there is no evidence that they come from a different population.
- 2 of the 20 new galaxies lie outside the v1 training range in at least one feature, so v2 covers a wider region of colour space. Test galaxies outside the training range: 4 in v1, 2 in v2.

## Test-set change (paired, same 20 galaxies)

- M1 Linear: RMSE 0.0410 → 0.0418 (Δ = +0.0007, +1.8%; paired 95% CI [-0.0021, +0.0029]; P(better) = 0.28; 10 of 20 galaxies closer). σ_NMAD 0.0320 → 0.0253.
- M2 k-NN: RMSE 0.0428 → 0.0376 (Δ = -0.0052, -12.2%; paired 95% CI [-0.0081, -0.0015]; P(better) = 1.00; 13 of 20 galaxies closer). σ_NMAD 0.0308 → 0.0319.
- M3 Random Forest: RMSE 0.0331 → 0.0318 (Δ = -0.0013, -4.0%; paired 95% CI [-0.0049, +0.0027]; P(better) = 0.76; 11 of 20 galaxies closer). σ_NMAD 0.0285 → 0.0276.
- M4 SVR: RMSE 0.0391 → 0.0444 (Δ = +0.0052, +13.4%; paired 95% CI [-0.0018, +0.0107]; P(better) = 0.09; 12 of 20 galaxies closer). σ_NMAD 0.0282 → 0.0284.
- Learners that improve: 2 of 4; with the whole paired CI below zero: 1.
- Best learner by test RMSE: M3 Random Forest in v1, M3 Random Forest in v2.
- Cross-validation RMSE (each version's own training set, so not paired): M1 Linear 0.0226 → 0.0238; M2 k-NN 0.0324 → 0.0324; M3 Random Forest 0.0305 → 0.0302; M4 SVR 0.0208 → 0.0217.

## Hyperparameters (T08)

- M2 k-NN: k 8 → 11.

## Reading the result

- With 20 test galaxies, each version's own RMSE CI is wide (T05). The paired CI removes the shared galaxy-to-galaxy scatter, so it is the right test of whether the extra training data helped.
- M1 Linear: **no clear change** (paired 95% CI [-0.0021, +0.0029] includes zero; P(better) = 0.28).
- M2 k-NN: **clear improvement** (paired 95% CI [-0.0081, -0.0015] lies below zero).
- M3 Random Forest: **no clear change** (paired 95% CI [-0.0049, +0.0027] includes zero; P(better) = 0.76).
- M4 SVR: **no clear change** (paired 95% CI [-0.0018, +0.0107] includes zero; P(better) = 0.09).
- Bias–variance reading: k-NN and the random forest predict from *local* averages of training galaxies, so with n = 80 their error is dominated by variance (how sparsely the colour–redshift relation is sampled). 25% more galaxies samples it more densely, and the CV-tuned k rose from 8 to 11: with denser data the model can average more neighbours without blurring the relation. Linear regression has 6 parameters and is limited by bias (a straight line through a curved relation), so extra data cannot help it. The tuned SVR kernel is very wide (σ = 0.01), which makes it close to linear, so it behaves like the linear model; its test change is within the noise.
- Learning curves (F22, v2): from 80 to 100 training galaxies the mean test RMSE changes by M1 Linear -0.0002, M2 k-NN +0.0002, M3 Random Forest -0.0002, M4 SVR +0.0034. No curve is still falling by more than 0.001 in RMSE, so further galaxies of the same kind would give only small gains: the remaining error is set mainly by how much redshift information five broad-band magnitudes carry (intrinsic scatter of the colour–redshift relation), not by the sample size.
